guard: a reusable user bearer cannot amplify connection nonces into unbounded public-KV watcher consumers; retained pairs stay capped across concurrency, lifecycle rotation, and auth-service restart, reclaim requires both exact consumers gone, and user-mode lifecycle teardown gains no authority over an unprovisioned pair
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/auth build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/manager exec tsc -p tsconfig.json && pnpm smoke:user-spawn:live
why: The live suite uses a real nats-server, real auth callout, real manager, and raw bearer
connections that never construct CotalEndpoint. The monitor is harness-only observability;
Mutations 1 and 2 independently remove the capacity test and the durable reserve-before-create
fence. Either must let the 40-nonce burst retain more than 32 pairs. Mutation 3 weakens BOTH-gone
to either-gone and must admit after only the presence half is deleted. Mutation 4 restores the
manager's unbindable lifecycle pair. Mutation 5 is the faster credential-matrix half: a user-mode
deprovisioner must not regain DELETE authority over a pair its lifecycle never provisioned.
The build and afterRestore commands are load-bearing: user-spawn imports core/auth/manager dist.

mutations.name: capacity removed: every fresh connection nonce can reserve another watcher pair
mutations.expectRed: concurrent nonce bursts admit exactly the documented number of unbound watcher pairs
mutations.cell: concurrent nonce bursts admit exactly the documented number of unbound watcher pairs
mutations.note: This restores the reported resource-amplification defect directly.

mutations.name: reserve-after-never: broker consumers are created without durable allocation rows
mutations.expectRed: concurrent nonce bursts admit exactly the documented number of unbound watcher pairs
mutations.cell: concurrent nonce bursts admit exactly the documented number of unbound watcher pairs
mutations.note: Without reserve-before-create, concurrent requests all observe spare capacity and leave uncounted consumers.

mutations.name: half-gone reclaim: one missing consumer is treated as the whole allocation gone
mutations.find:
await jsm.consumers.info(stream, agentKvWatchConsumerName(kind, args.owner, args.actor, watchUid));
            return false;
mutations.replace:
await jsm.consumers.info(stream, agentKvWatchConsumerName(kind, args.owner, args.actor, watchUid));
            continue;
mutations.expectRed: one surviving consumer keeps its allocation occupied (reclaim requires BOTH exact names gone)
mutations.cell: one surviving consumer keeps its allocation occupied (reclaim requires BOTH exact names gone)
mutations.note: A pair is one allocation; either retained member must keep its slot occupied.

mutations.name: managed user mode again provisions an unbindable lifecycle watcher pair
mutations.replace:
// MUTANT: restore the unbindable lifecycle-named pair.
          lifecycleKvWatches: true,
mutations.expectRed: a managed user-mode spawn provisions only its bindable connection-owned watcher pair
mutations.cell: a managed user-mode spawn provisions only its bindable connection-owned watcher pair
mutations.note: The endpoint derives its watcher UID from the connection nonce, so this lifecycle pair has no binder.

mutations.name: user-mode teardown regains DELETE authority over an unprovisioned lifecycle watcher pair
mutations.expectRed: a user-mode deprovisioner is NOT granted delete on an unprovisioned lifecycle presence watcher
mutations.cell: a user-mode deprovisioner is NOT granted delete on an unprovisioned lifecycle presence watcher
mutations.note: The permission mint and teardown footprint must stay coherent for user mode.
